artboards.title: Today · a stop with a note
Planner · a stop selected, two drags in flight

annotations.text:
THE WAY IN

Sign in, then Trips, then New trip, then the trip opens on Today.

New trip asks two things: a name and the dates. Nothing else.

On the Trips cards the line under the name lists the cities the trip's stops are in, worked out from the places themselves. A trip with nothing in it yet shows only its dates, which is what Portugal looks like here.

The G mark on the sign-in button is a PLACEHOLDER for the asset Google ships.

THE STOP MENU, AND ADDING PLACES

The kebab holds exactly two things: Move to date, which opens the sheet beside it, and Remove from list. Navigate, Visited and Add note stay on the row where they are used constantly.

Search is biased to the open day, not the whole planet. Places API takes a locationBias circle of up to 50 km, centred on that day's stops, and the radius is a chip you can widen. Results outside it still appear, greyed, with the distance.

Sign-in is Google. Drive is a separate, later consent, asked only when you first attach a file.

PLANNER

Click any empty cell and the search opens right there, already scoped to that day and that hour. The sidebar is To be planned: uncollapsed, scrollable, everything not on a day yet. Two rows along the bottom: travel and where you sleep.

The plus at each end of the grid extends the trip by a day, so a trip that runs long or gets cut short is a click rather than a settings screen. The arrows by the view switcher page through a trip too long to fit.

Three ways to shape the day list. A is what the app screens are built on, because it is what you described. B and C are here so you can see what you are giving up. They are sketches, not proposals - say the word and I will build one out properly.

PLANNER · SELECTION AND DRAG

Clicking an event opens the same three actions the phone has, in a popover beside it: Edit, Add note, Delete. It says Edit note once there is one.

Two drags are shown at once, which would not happen in life but shows both halves. On Sat Oct 3 an event already on the grid is being moved up its own day, with a dashed ghost left where it was. On Mon Oct 5 an item is being dragged in from To be planned, and its row in the sidebar is dashed out until it lands. Both show a green drop line with the time it would take, and dragging across columns moves the day.
